body.statement: Every symbolic formula returned by \(\operatorname{Branch\text{-}sCIDP}(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\) equals \(\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c)\) for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\). The role graph has at most \(2^{|X\cup C|}\) states, every nonrepeating trace has length at most \(2^{|X\cup C|}-1\), and the shared formula DAG can be constructed in \(O(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)+L_{\mathrm{form}})\) symbolic operations. No implication from \(\operatorname{AllFail}\) to nonidentification is asserted here.
body.justification: Exhaustive legal exchanges preserve the target and isolate the converse difficulty without sacrificing a usable positive identification procedure.
body.gap: Chen--Mooij prove soundness for their conditional procedure; the branch closure and shared-cache accounting are not stated as this explicit formula-search theorem.
body.consumer: PAGId can return selected-cohort formulas with a finite auditable role trace even before a complete failure theorem is available.
body.proof_tex:
For a represented model \(\mathbf M\), write
\[
 \mathcal X_A(\mathbf M)
 :=\prod_{v\in A}\operatorname{supp}_{\mathbf M}(V_v)
\]
for the finite discrete state space of an observed set \(A\subseteq V\); for
\(A=\varnothing\) this is the singleton containing the empty assignment.  Put
\(W=X\cup C\).  If \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\) is a role state, let
\(\bar x\) and \(\bar c\) be the restrictions of the original assignment
\((x,c)\) to \(\bar X\) and \(\bar C\), respectively, and define the
proof-local kernel
\[
 K_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y)
 :=P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 Y=y\mid \operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x),
 \bar C=\bar c,S=\mathbf 1\right).
 \tag{1}
\]
The sets in (1) are well typed and disjoint: by
\(\mathrm{ass{:}disjoint\text{-}query\text{-}sets}\),
\(Y\cap W=\varnothing\), and by the definition of a role state,
\(\bar X\mathbin{\dot\cup}\bar C=W\).  The model hypothesis
\(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\text{-}discrete\text{-}selected\text{-}model}\)
places \(\mathbf M\) in \(\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\).  Thus all discrete
point masses used below are pointwise versions, and, at each assignment under
consideration,
\[
 P_{\mathbf M}(\bar C=\bar c,S=\mathbf 1
       \mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x))>0.
 \tag{2}
\]
When \(\bar C=\varnothing\), the corresponding conditional mass after
conditioning on \(S=\mathbf 1\) is one.  Equation (2) is the positivity premise
needed for every conditioning and division below.

We first establish invariance along every edge of the role graph.  At its root
\(\rho_0=(X,C)\), \(\mathrm{def{:}target\text{-}query}\) gives
\[
 K_{\rho_0,\mathbf M}(y)
 =P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c,S=\mathbf 1)
 =\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c).
 \tag{3}
\]
Suppose an edge from \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\) moves the nonempty current
bucket intersection \(T\subseteq\bar X\) from treatment to conditioning.
By \(\mathrm{def{:}reachable\text{-}role\text{-}graph}\), that edge exists
only if its Rule--2 separation holds.  Apply
\(\mathrm{lem{:}selected\text{-}rule\text{-}two}\) with
\[
 A_0=Y,\qquad B_0=T,\qquad C_0=\bar C,
 \qquad D_0=\bar X\setminus T.
\]
These four sets are pairwise disjoint by the role partition and
\(Y\cap W=\varnothing\).  The Rule--2 equality is therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 K_{(\bar X,\bar C),\mathbf M}(y)
 &=P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 Y=y\mid T=\bar x_T,\bar C=\bar c,
 \operatorname{do}(\bar X\setminus T=\bar x_{\bar X\setminus T}),
 S=\mathbf 1\right)\\
 &=K_{(\bar X\setminus T,\,\bar C\cup T),\mathbf M}(y).
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{4}
\]
If instead an edge moves nonempty \(T\subseteq\bar C\) from conditioning to
treatment, apply the same lemma with
\[
 A_0=Y,\qquad B_0=T,\qquad C_0=\bar C\setminus T,
 \qquad D_0=\bar X.
\]
Reading its equality in the reverse direction gives
\[
 K_{(\bar X,\bar C),\mathbf M}(y)
 =K_{(\bar X\cup T,\,\bar C\setminus T),\mathbf M}(y).
 \tag{5}
\]
Induction on the finite number of edges in a trace, using (3)--(5), yields
\[
 K_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y)=\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c)
 \quad\text{for every reachable }\rho.
 \tag{6}
\]

Now suppose Branch-sCIDP succeeds at
\(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\).  The terminal sIDP call has outcome set
\(A_0=Y\cup\bar C\) and intervention set \(B_0=\bar X\).  They are disjoint,
and \(A_0\ne\varnothing\) by
\(\mathrm{ass{:}nonempty\text{-}outcome}\).  The pointwise positive-discrete
specialization in \(\mathrm{lem{:}sidp\text{-}soundness}\) therefore gives
\[
 F_\rho(y,\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})
 =J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y,\bar c;\bar x)
 \quad
 \text{for all }y\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M).
 \tag{7}
\]
This invocation is directly on \(\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\); it does not
infer positive identification from the binary rational certificate subclass.
Finite support marginalization of (7), followed by the corrected definition
of \(D_\rho\), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sum_{y'\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)}
 F_\rho(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})\\
 &\qquad=\sum_{y'\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)}
 J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y',\bar c;\bar x)\\
 &\qquad=P_{\mathbf M}(\bar C=\bar c
       \mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x),S=\mathbf 1)
 =D_{\rho,\mathbf M}(\bar c;\bar x)>0,
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{8}
\]
where the final inequality is (2) after division by the positive selection
mass.  Dividing (7) by (8), applying the definition of conditional
probability, and then using (6), we obtain
\[
 \frac{F_\rho(y,\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})}
 {\sum_{y'\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)}
   F_\rho(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})}
 =K_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y)
 =\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c).
 \tag{9}
\]
Thus the normalized expression is an observed-law identifying map for the
causal target; equality was derived from Rule--2 and sIDP soundness and was not
introduced as a definition.  No division is attempted when sIDP fails.

It remains to establish the finite-search and cache bounds.  A role state is
uniquely determined by \(\bar X\subseteq W\), because
\(\bar C=W\setminus\bar X\).  Hence
\[
 |\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)|\le 2^{|W|}=2^{|X\cup C|}.
 \tag{10}
\]
A nonrepeating trace with \(r\) visited states has \(r-1\) edges, so (10)
implies a maximum trace length of \(2^{|X\cup C|}-1\).

For the outer enumeration, each visited state tests at most two directions for
each of at most \(n\) buckets.  The manipulated graph has \(O(n)\) observed
and regime vertices and \(O(n^2)\) marked adjacencies.  The required
separation test is a reachability search on the finite graph of admissible
edge-incidence states, and anterior closure, bucket construction, and region
construction are likewise finite graph searches.  Each test therefore costs
\(\operatorname{poly}(n)\), so the outer search costs
\[
 O\!\left(2^n\operatorname{poly}(n)\right).
 \tag{11}
\]

By \(\mathrm{lem{:}sidp\text{-}recursion\text{-}structure}\), a deterministic
BuildTree subproblem is keyed by one subset \(R\subseteq V\), while a fixing
subproblem is keyed by a pair \(R\subseteq T_0\subseteq V\).  There are at
most \(2^n\) keys of the first kind, and
\[
 \#\{(R,T_0):R\subseteq T_0\subseteq V\}
 =\sum_{T_0\subseteq V}2^{|T_0|}
 =(1+2)^n=3^n.
 \tag{12}
\]
The equality in (12) also follows by assigning each vertex independently to
\(R\), \(T_0\setminus R\), or \(V\setminus T_0\).  The same lemma shows that
BuildTree descends to proper children and every successful fixing iteration
strictly removes a nonempty bucket.  Thus every deterministic key terminates,
is evaluated once under \(\mathrm{def{:}shared\text{-}formula\text{-}cache}\),
and performs only \(\operatorname{poly}(n)\) graph work.  Equations (11) and
(12) consequently bound all cached graph computation by
\[
 O\!\left(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)\right).
 \tag{13}
\]
Finally, each marginalization, product, quotient, and assembly operation is a
constant-arity node of the shared formula DAG.  Constructing and writing these
nodes costs \(O(L_{\mathrm{form}})\) by the definition of
\(L_{\mathrm{form}}\).  Combining this with (13) proves the advertised
\[
 O\!\left(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)+L_{\mathrm{form}}\right)
\]
bound.  The argument used only successful terminal calls, so it establishes no
implication from \(\operatorname{AllFail}\) to nonidentification.
